title: The Hungry Harvest
premise: Folklorist Ansel Ashgrove arrives in the dying village of Harrow's Bend to record its harvest songs, only to hear a church bell that was melted down in 1911 toll across the fields at dusk. The villagers, bound by a pact renewed every generation, recognize him as the 'returner' foretold in their songs — the one who must give back what was taken in 1974: his own mother's voice, stolen when she fled the village pregnant with him. As the harvest moon swells, Ansel uncovers that the village's abundance has been fed by sacrificed voices, and that his documentation — his careful, loving records — is itself the mechanism by which the harvest remembers and claims. In the climax he chooses truth over survival, singing his mother's stolen song back to the fields and shattering the pact, though the price is his own recorded memory of her; the village withers honestly at last, and Ansel leaves voiceless but free.
about_author: K. M. Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging disappearing regional folk music across the American Midwest. They write horror about what communities bury to keep breathing.

chapters.title: Songs They Won't Sing Twice
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. He arrives in Harrow's Bend, charming the elderly into recording harvest songs that they perform exactly once, then deny ever singing. The songs all end mid-verse at the same word: 'return.' Emotional beat: scholarly delight curdling into unease as he realizes the villagers are frightened of their own music.

chapters.title: The Bell That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At dusk a bell tolls; the church has no bell, melted down in 1911 according to parish records Ansel himself verified. Villagers shutter their windows and whisper that 'the returner has come.' Emotional beat: vertigo — his rational worldview cracks as the impossible rings in his own ears.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with an interleaf of the village ledger. In the archive he finds entries from 1974: a woman named Mara Ashgrove, listed not as a resident but as 'taken — voice, one.' His surname. Emotional beat: dread of inheritance, the first hint that his trip was never coincidence.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Fed the Field
chapters.summary: Alternating Ansel and old Wren Halloway's POV. Wren confesses the pact: each generation gives a voice to the fields, and the harvest never fails. 1974's offering escaped, and the land has been starving ever since, growing bitter grain and hungrier songs. Emotional beat: horrified compassion — the villagers are perpetrators and victims at once.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. He plays back his recordings and hears his own voice answering questions he never asked, in a cadence not his own. His tapes are filling with the village's memories, and his own are thinning. Emotional beat: the horror of his devotion turned weapon — his archive is eating him.

chapters.title: Mara's Verse
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals the full song of 1974: Mara was meant to be given, but she sang a counter-verse that broke the rite and fled, pregnant. The fields have been waiting for her blood to come back and finish the verse. Emotional beat: grief and awe — Ansel's mother out-sang a god, briefly.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Rises Half
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Half-moon: the village turns on him gently, lovingly, offering warmth and bread, insisting he stay and 'sing the closing verse' willingly. He finds his car dead, roads looping back. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tenderness — captivity dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: Return What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In the bell-less tower he finds the 1911 bell's clapper buried in grain, and within it, a preserved thread of Mara's voice. To return it he must sing her counter-verse — but singing it will cost him his own recorded memories of her. Emotional beat: the loyalty/truth collision — keep her memory or free everyone.

chapters.title: The Counter-Verses
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, climax. Under the full harvest moon, the villagers gather him in the field. He sings Mara's verse, returns her voice to the clapper, and the bell tolls one final time — a sound that unmakes the pact. The fields exhale; the hunger ends. His tapes go blank. Emotional beat: terrible, triumphant release.

chapters.title: The Withering, Honestly
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, epilogue. Spring: Harrow's Bend grows thin, honest crops; some villagers leave, some stay to farm the poor soil and finally sing their songs freely, twice and more. Ansel, unable to recall his mother's face, writes the last entry in his notebook by hand: 'Some prayers are answered by taking them back.' Emotional beat: mournful peace — survival's price paid, truth kept.
